detail.runner_up_case: ADVERSE rests on a single alleged material fact: the OFAC SDN designation of 16 Sep 2025 (IFSR/SDGT). No criminal conviction, insolvency, major civil judgment or regulatory enforcement surfaced in court_records or web searches, so if the sanctions fact fails, nothing else supports ADVERSE. That fact is weaker than it appears: the only corroboration (cus.com.cy) is a newsletter reprinting the OFAC notice, not an independent second source, so Q7/Q10 are technically unsatisfied; the sanctionssearch.ofac.treas.gov hit is an undated snapshot that cannot by itself prove the listing still stood on 2026-09-30; and OFAC has previously delisted EO 13224 designees after administrative review, so a revocation between Sep 2025 and Oct 2026 would make the present-tense 'is sanctioned' claim false as of the as-of date. On that narrow basis NO_ADVERSE is arguable. It is, however, a weak case that I cannot honestly recommend: the designated record matches the subject on legal name, Arabic name, Dubai jurisdiction and registration number 930153, so a namesake defense is effectively foreclosed, and an SDN listing is by definition a material adverse fact under the verdict vocabulary.
